Pricing comparison

CardScanFox vs CollX: what does the price represent?

CardScanFox is an option for tracking confirmed holdings by printing, condition and existing grade. CollX also documents a marketplace workflow. Compare the meaning of each price and the task you need; no accuracy winner has been established here.

CardScanFox is available on iPhone and Android. Both stores currently list it as Card AI: TCG Card Scanner.

DownloadApp Store DownloadGoogle Play

How should I choose between CardScanFox and CollX?

  1. Decide whether you need reviewed holdings, a marketplace workflow, or both. Read the dated official sources linked below for each documented difference.
  2. Use known cards to check printing selection. Include the raw conditions and existing slab grades you actually own.
  3. In CardScanFox, confirm the set, full card number, language and finish. Enter the condition or existing grade before adding a holding.
  4. Read the available price with its date and context. A market reference, a recent transaction and a listing ask can answer different questions.

Correct a wrong candidate before saving it. If the exact printing or its price is unavailable, do not use another printing or a zero amount. We have not measured recognition or valuation accuracy on matched physical cards; this is a workflow comparison.

Variant, condition and price are separate decisions

A useful test with two copies of one card

Take one raw copy and one PSA slab of the same printing. In each app, confirm the exact variant, enter the raw condition or slab grade, and note whether the displayed figure is a current estimate, a last sale or a historical trend. This makes an appraisal question concrete. Neither a scanner result nor a marketplace estimate authenticates the card.

CollX is a fit if its built-in buy, sell and trade workflow matters to you. CardScanFox focuses on reviewed catalog records, condition-specific holdings and collection value. Both products support sports cards; neither should be described as uniquely supporting them.

Read the source of the number

CollX explains its median, fallback and estimate rules in its pricing FAQ. CardScanFox shows its published market price and available history; an eBay link for sports cards opens a separate search and is not a synced feed of sold transactions. Comparing those figures as if they are the same metric can mislead a seller.

Sources were reviewed November 24, 2026. We have not measured recognition or valuation accuracy on matched physical cards.

Compare scanning modes and memberships

CardScanFox accepts one card per browser photo and queues up to 10 separate photos in its mobile app. CollX documents Single Scan for one card and Batch mode for adding multiple scans to a collection. Its November release notes also describe a choice between front-only and front-and-back capture.

CollX offers a free app with a collection limit. Its site lists Pro at $9.99 per month with unlimited collection items and 500 monthly Scan+ credits. Gold is $24.99 per month and lists unlimited Scan+ and additional seller tools. Scan+ is CollX's enhanced identification mode. Compare those credits with CardScanFox’s successful-scan allowance as separate measures.

CardScanFox vs CollX questions.

How many free scans does CardScanFox include?

The iPhone app includes 10 successful free scans per account or guest identity, with no daily or monthly reset. The 10-image queue is the number of separate images you can review together. Check the current Premium offer in the app for its price and terms.

Does CollX identify raw card condition automatically?

CollX documents manual condition entry and detecting whether a card is raw or already graded. CardScanFox collection records use the raw condition or existing slab grade you enter. Its separate web pregrading estimates visible condition from two photos.

Can I use both apps for sports cards?

Both document sports-card scanning. CardScanFox also has catalog records for Pokémon, Magic, One Piece and Yu-Gi-Oh! Check that the exact printing and price are available in the category you need.

Are CardScanFox and CollX prices calculated the same way?

Do not assume so. CollX publishes a median and fallback methodology in its FAQ. CardScanFox shows a published market price and available history for the selected record; its eBay search link is separate.
